callout.text: fastest route from A to B

storyboard.addedInformation: The road makes 'fastest route from A to B' literal; his glare shows the loathing for slow people.
storyboard.claim: Reds decide they know the fastest route and loathe waiting for slow people.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stuart jabbing a finger down a straight road stretching from A to B, impatient and glaring.
storyboard.onScreenText: fastest route from A to B
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the Red-boss portrait: why he wants to be in charge.

storyboard.addedInformation: His pointing at a clock-free, people-directed gesture shows control is about tempo, not prestige.
storyboard.claim: Reds seek control only to control the pace.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stuart pointing sharply at his team as if setting their tempo, office behind him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers beat 80: control is the tool, pace is the goal.

storyboard.addedInformation: The papers in his hand name the only currency he respects: delivered work, not affection.
storyboard.claim: A Red does not care if you like him, only that the work lands on time.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stuart holding up spreadsheet papers, stern and businesslike, approval nowhere on his face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Widens beat 81: approval is irrelevant, delivery is everything.

storyboard.addedInformation: The target behind the cut-off shows what the interruption serves: the finish line, not friendship.
storyboard.claim: Reds cut meetings short to demand the bottom line and cross the finish line.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stuart cutting off a seated colleague with a raised hand, a finish-line target beside them.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From principle to scene: the meeting cut-off in action.

storyboard.addedInformation: The struck phrase rejects the insult; the explainer's calm face reframes it as an untranslated need.
storyboard.claim: That pushy colleague is not an idiot or a sociopath, just an untranslated need for speed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Erikson calmly explaining to camera while the words 'an idiot' are struck through.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Verdict on the Red sequence before pivoting to the opposite energy.

storyboard.addedInformation: Her laughing entrance embodies the claim; the hosts hand the scene to her by name.
storyboard.claim: If Red is the engine of speed, Yellow is the engine of enthusiasm: meet Marita.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marita laughing mid-gesture in a living room as Erikson introduces her as his Yellow sister.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivot from Red speed to its polar opposite: Yellow energy.

storyboard.addedInformation: Her bright blouse and laugh against a pitch-black window stage sunshine inside darkness.
storyboard.claim: Marita is pure Yellow, pure sunshine, even with pitch black outside.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marita beaming in a lamplit living room, the window behind her pitch black.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Defines Marita before the storm scene tests her.

storyboard.addedInformation: The storm icon shows the violence outside; her calm smile already hints it cannot touch her.
storyboard.claim: Rain lashes the windows and thunder shakes the floorboards in a miserable storm.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A violent storm raging outside the living-room window while Marita sits calmly on the sofa.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets the apocalyptic backdrop her optimism will defy.

storyboard.addedInformation: Her pointing at the black window with a laugh stages the exact quoted moment.
storyboard.claim: Marita sits cross-legged, laughing, pointing at the black window: don't worry.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marita cross-legged on the sofa, laughing and pointing at the dark stormy window.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The storm's payoff: her laughing response to it.

storyboard.addedInformation: Her sincere warmth shows this is belief, not sarcasm, per the negation rule.
storyboard.claim: She means it without sarcasm: the sun will come out any minute.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marita speaking with warm sincere conviction, hand on heart, no trace of a smirk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reframes beat 88: the laugh was genuine belief, not sarcasm.

storyboard.addedInformation: Her animated people-facing chatter performs the textbook Yellow definition.
storyboard.claim: Yellows believe it on a cellular level: extroverted and people oriented.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marita chatting animatedly, turned toward people, radiating outward energy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From one scene to the general rule it proves.

storyboard.addedInformation: Her raised arms drinking in applause show optimism and energy have a fuel: attention.
storyboard.claim: Yellows run on optimism, high-voltage energy, and applause.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marita beaming with arms raised as if soaking up applause.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the fuel behind the sunshine.

storyboard.addedInformation: Her stride into a gray sterile room performs the injection; the room's drabness is the before.
storyboard.claim: Yellows walk into a sterile conference room and inject life into it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marita sweeping into a gray sterile conference room, color and laughter arriving with her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows her gift at work, then hints at its price.

storyboard.addedInformation: The idea-bulb plus her clutch of sketches counts the five concepts; lunch is still ahead.
storyboard.claim: A Yellow enthusiastically conceives five world-changing projects before lunch.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marita eagerly pitching beside a glowing idea bulb, project sketches fanning from her hand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The trade-off begins: conception at full voltage.

storyboard.addedInformation: Her slump over scattered detail pages shows execution draining her; the papers are the kryptonite.
storyboard.claim: She may finish a fraction of one: execution needs detail focus, and details are kryptonite.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marita deflated over a desk of scattered detail pages, one half-finished sheet among many.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The bill for beat 93: ideas without follow-through.

storyboard.addedInformation: Her bright distracted sparkle toward something new performs the dopamine wiring.
storyboard.claim: Her dopamine system is wired for novelty and social connection, not follow-through.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marita lighting up at something new off-screen, half-turned from unfinished work.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains beats 93-94: the wiring behind the pattern.

storyboard.addedInformation: The bundle of cards in her hands is the footprint: sociability you can count.
storyboard.claim: Spot a Yellow by the footprint: massive stacks of holiday cards sent and received.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marita gleefully holding a tall stack of holiday cards, more piles around her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Field guide begins: how to spot one in the wild.

storyboard.addedInformation: The phone in hand plus her hug-ready arms stages thousands of contacts as warmth, not tech.
storyboard.claim: Thousands of contacts, maxed-out Facebook: a stranger is just a friend not yet hugged.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marita clutching her phone, arms open mid-hug toward a newcomer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the footprint: from cards to contacts.

storyboard.addedInformation: Her self-pointing storytelling pose performs the I-centered hero narration.
storyboard.claim: Yellows are storytellers, usually the hero, saying I constantly.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marita mid-story, thumb pointed at herself, laughing at her own tale.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From social volume to verbal style.

storyboard.addedInformation: The colleague's flat-tire tale dies unheard as she leans in to reclaim the story.
storyboard.claim: Tell her about your flat tire and she listens four seconds before the I flood.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marita leaning in, about to interrupt, while a colleague starts his flat-tire story.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Demonstrates the I-habit on a concrete anecdote.

storyboard.addedInformation: Her epic arm-sweep dwarfs his slump: the hijack's scale is the insult task-people feel.
storyboard.claim: She hijacks it with a twenty-minute epic about her transmission exploding on a bridge.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marita holding court with a sweeping bridge-disaster gesture while her colleague slumps, unheard.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hijack lands; the colleague's story is gone.

storyboard.addedInformation: The host's level stare voices the pushback honestly: many find this archetype draining.
storyboard.claim: The hosts push back: honestly, this archetype is kind of exhausting.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Erikson facing camera with a candid, measured look, voicing the audience fatigue.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hosts pause the portrait to admit the cost.

storyboard.addedInformation: His slump under her chatter (worried plus slump, never talk) stages quiet drained wariness.
storyboard.claim: Relentless optimism and self-referential stories feel deeply manipulative.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A drained colleague slumped at his desk as cheerful chatter washes over him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sharpens beat 101: exhaustion curdles into suspicion.

storyboard.addedInformation: The mask plus her edged smirk stages the suspicion itself: is the sunshine worn?
storyboard.claim: Are they faking the sunshine just to stay the center of attention?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marita with a performative bright smile beside a mask, charm with an edge.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The accusation stated outright: faked happiness for status.

storyboard.addedInformation: Striking the phrase rejects the analytical critique while crediting who levels it.
storyboard.claim: Critics call it toxic positivity, but science says they are not faking it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Erikson calmly striking through the words toxic positivity as he cites the science.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the critique to dismantle it.

storyboard.addedInformation: His focused think-pose performs the filter at work: tuning toward the positive.
storyboard.claim: Their brain filter prioritizes positive social stimuli and screens the rest.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Erikson in a focused think-pose, attention visibly tuning toward bright social signals.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The mechanism: the reticular activating system.

storyboard.addedInformation: Her unguarded celebration shows brightness as habitat, not act.
storyboard.claim: Negative data gets screened out: their reality is genuinely that bright.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marita glowing with genuine delight in a bright room, shadows simply absent.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Verdict on the fakery question: it is real to them.

storyboard.addedInformation: The storm swirling around her while the organized colleague braces shows the Blue-eye view.
storyboard.claim: To an organized Blue, a Yellow looks like a tornado of chaos and missed deadlines.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marita cheerfully whirling amid a storm of flying papers while a colleague braces against it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Concedes the Blue critique before defending Yellow utility.

storyboard.addedInformation: Her energy lifting his burnt-out slump shows logic failing where enthusiasm succeeds.
storyboard.claim: When Red has burnt the team out, only Yellow energy gets ideas off the ground again.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marita rallying a burnt-out slumped team while charts of logic lie ignored.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The defense: what Yellows are for after Red damage.

storyboard.addedInformation: Her paddles-up rallying jolt over a flatlined team stages the metaphor without a medical prop.
storyboard.claim: Yellows are the organizational defibrillator, the ultimate hype man.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marita jolting a flatlined, depleted team back to life with pure rallying energy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Coins the slogan for beat 108 rescue.

storyboard.addedInformation: Her tangent-telling glee reframes the derailment: static on the enthusiasm frequency.
storyboard.claim: When she derails your agenda with a tangent, she broadcasts pure enthusiasm, not idiocy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Marita gleefully off on a tangent mid-meeting, radiating enthusiasm while the agenda waits.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reframes the annoyance: tangent as broadcast.

storyboard.addedInformation: The four-color grid with only Red and Yellow lit shows the missing foundation.
storyboard.claim: A company of only Reds and Yellows would burn to the ground in chaos.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The four-color grid with the Red and Yellow quadrants blazing and the rest dark, Erikson gesturing at the gap.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The warning: two colors alone cannot hold.

storyboard.addedInformation: The flow from chaos to foundation diagrams the argument: Green is what the first two lack.
storyboard.claim: That is why we need the structural foundation of Green, the most common profile.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A calm seated colleague anchoring the frame as the flow resolves from Red-Yellow chaos to Green foundation.
storyboard.onScreenText: Reds and Yellows lead to Green foundation
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Structural pivot: from the two extroverts to the missing base.

storyboard.addedInformation: The stand-in seated at the reception desk introduces Maya the Green without inventing a face.
storyboard.claim: Introverted and people oriented, Green is society's bedrock: meet Maya at reception.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A calm receptionist seated at a consulting-firm desk, steady and welcoming.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the third color through its representative.

storyboard.addedInformation: The paper piles swallowing the monitor make the disaster zone countable.
storyboard.claim: Her workspace is a disaster zone: a tectonic plate of paper and sticky notes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A desk buried under sliding piles of papers and sticky notes, the monitor barely visible.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the Green workspace: chaos by kindness, not by hype.

storyboard.addedInformation: Her open nodding acceptance of yet another file performs the yes-reflex.
storyboard.claim: You can barely see her monitor because she says yes to absolutely every request.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The receptionist nodding yes as another request lands on the pile.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the pile: every yes added a sheet.

storyboard.addedInformation: Her slump beneath the workload (worried plus slump) stages drowning without water imagery.
storyboard.claim: She lacks the capacity to say no, yet drowns in an unmanageable workload.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The receptionist slumped beneath her towering workload, still accepting more.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the mechanism: the missing no.

storyboard.addedInformation: The cup in her hand plus the plumped cushion stages hospitality amid overload.
storyboard.claim: Still, she gets up to brew fresh coffee and plump the waiting-area cushions.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The receptionist carrying a fresh cup across the waiting area, straightening a cushion.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The paradox: service continues as the pile grows.

storyboard.addedInformation: The small gift box makes the secret email concrete: care for juniors' families.
storyboard.claim: She secretly emails stressed juniors to remind them about a spouse's birthday gift.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The receptionist quietly wrapping a small birthday gift amid her paper piles.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Deepens beat 117: hidden care beyond the coffee.

storyboard.addedInformation: Her calm settled presence among colleagues stages herd safety without literal animals.
storyboard.claim: Greens prioritize stability, harmony, and kindness: fierce dedication to the herd.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The calm colleague settled warmly among coworkers, the steady center of the group.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Maya's scenes to the Green rule they prove.
